title: The opacity alibi: when “too complex” stops the questions
standfirst: A machine-checked result is not a lesson learned. Before declaring AI discoveries beyond human understanding, we should ask whether we have tested understanding fairly.
summary: An enormous proof, a deceptively simple switch puzzle and two identical-looking causal worlds reveal why checking a result and understanding it are different achievements.
claimBoundary: An accessible adaptation of The Opacity Alibi research prospectus, with standard constructed parity and causal-identification examples. No human study, frontier-model evaluation, demonstrated audit advantage or universal limit on human understanding is reported. Commentary does not imply external peer review or formal verification.

banner.alt: A random signal controls X which controls Y, or controls Y which controls X. Observations agree, but forcing X on makes Y certainly on in the first and on half the time in the second.
banner.caption: Constructed causal schematic, not experimental data. Both models produce matching lights; forcing X on distinguishes their predictions. The two answers are conditional on exactly these two models.
